
{{alias}}( N, searchElement, x, strideX )
    Returns the first index of an element in a double-precision complex
    floating-point strided array which is not equal to a specified search
    element.

    The `N` and stride parameters determine which elements in the strided array
    are accessed at runtime.

    Indexing is relative to the first index. To introduce an offset, use a typed
    array view.

    If `N <= 0`, the function returns `-1`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    N: integer
        Number of indexed elements.

    searchElement: Complex128
        Search element.

    x: Complex128Array
        Input array.

    strideX: integer
        Stride length.

    Returns
    -------
    idx: integer
        Index.

    Examples
    --------
    // Standard usage:
    > var x = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/complex128}}( [ 1.0, 2.0, 1.0, 2.0, 0.0, 0.0 ] );
    > var s = new {{alias:@stdlib/complex/float64/ctor}}( 1.0, 2.0 );
    > var idx = {{alias}}( x.length, s, x, 1 )
    2

    // Using `N` and stride parameters:
    > x = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/complex128}}( [ 1.0, 2.0, 9.0, 9.0, 0.0, 0.0, 9.0, 9.0 ] );
    > idx = {{alias}}( 2, s, x, 2 )
    1

    // View offsets:
    > var x0 = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/complex128}}( [ 9.0, 9.0, 1.0, 2.0, 0.0, 0.0 ] );
    > var x1 = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/complex128}}( x0.buffer, x0.BYTES_PER_ELEMENT*1 );
    > idx = {{alias}}( 2, s, x1, 1 )
    1


{{alias}}.ndarray( N, searchElement, x, strideX, offsetX )
    Returns the first index of an element in a double-precision complex
    floating-point strided array which is not equal to a specified search
    element using alternative indexing semantics.

    While typed array views mandate a view offset based on the underlying
    buffer, the offset parameter supports indexing semantics based on a
    starting index.

    Parameters
    ----------
    N: integer
        Number of indexed elements.

    searchElement: Complex128
        Search element.

    x: Complex128Array
        Input array.

    strideX: integer
        Stride length.

    offsetX: integer
        Starting index.

    Returns
    -------
    idx: integer
        Index.

    Examples
    --------
    // Standard usage:
    > var x = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/complex128}}( [ 1.0, 2.0, 1.0, 2.0, 0.0, 0.0 ] );
    > var s = new {{alias:@stdlib/complex/float64/ctor}}( 1.0, 2.0 );
    > var idx = {{alias}}.ndarray( x.length, s, x, 1, 0 )
    2

    // Advanced indexing:
    > x = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/complex128}}( [ 9.0, 9.0, 1.0, 2.0, 9.0, 9.0, 0.0, 0.0 ] );
    > idx = {{alias}}.ndarray( 2, s, x, 2, 1 )
    1

    See Also
    --------
